newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Alcatel Altech wins bulk of Telkom award.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Alcatel Altech wins bulk of Telkom award.

text.p: Franco-South African firm Alcatel Altech Telecoms (AAT) has won the bulk of a giant two billion rand radio technology contract from Telkom, the telecommunications utility said on Wednesday.
On Tuesday Telkom announced the tender award to AAT and U.S. firm Lucent Technologies Inc, but the exact split of the deal had not yet been decided.

The two year contract covers the supply, planning and installation of standalone Digital Enhanced Cordless Telecommunications (DECT) systems and Time Division Multiple Access (TDMA) with DECT tail systems.
On Wednesday Telkom said in statement that 90 percent of the TDMA contact had been awarded to AAT, with the remaining 10 percent going to Lucent.
On the DECT contract, the exact proportions had not been worked out yet but Telkom said that AAT would secure between 50 and 60 percent and Lucent between 40 and 50 percent.
Details of the exact areas where the systems will be rolled out will be finalised in due course.

Bill Venter, chairman of Altron, the controlling shareholder in Allied Technologies Ltd (Altech) which owns 40 percent of AAT said earlier that its unit expected to secure more than half of the tender.
AAT's other shareholders are France's Alcatel, with 40 percent, and black investment group Rethabile with 20 percent.
Speculation was rife on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange earlier that South African electronics firm Plessey Corp Ltd is to sign a deal with Lucent.
Following a cautionary notice on the market's trading system earlier, Plessey shares surged 102 cents to close at 946 cents.
